chunks: From him, from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, upon them be peace, who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: "When one of you is in financial hardship, let him go out (to seek livelihood) and not grieve himself and his family."

key_terms.أَعْسَرَ: To be in financial difficulty or insolvency

ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do when facing financial hardship according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of *tahdhib-al-ahkam*'s chapter on earnings, this hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq emphasizes proactive engagement in livelihood rather than passive resignation, linking financial struggle to the spiritual burden on one's family. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that seeking halal sustenance is an act of worship that preserves the dignity and peace of the household, preventing the anxiety of idleness from becoming a source of communal distress.
